name: keycloak
description: Example identity provider: Keycloak, which provides "oidc" (D19): each brick that requires it gets its own confidential client (OIDC_TOKEN_URL, OIDC_CLIENT_ID, OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET), with the realm "plugbricks" (roles plugbricks-admin and plugbricks-viewer, the admin's public client), no user. Its console is published on 127.0.0.1:<webPort>/admin/; sign in as admin with the generated password in .secrets/secrets.env (PB_KEYCLOAK__ADMIN_PASSWORD), create the users there, then run plugbricks admin --issuer http://127.0.0.1:<webPort>/realms/plugbricks --client-id plugbricks-admin. Its source is apis/keycloak; build the image with: docker build -t plugbricks-example/keycloak:0.1.0 apis/keycloak

exec:
exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8080 && printf 'GET /realms/plugbricks/.well-known/openid-configuration HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Connection: close

' >&3 && head -n 1 <&3 | grep -q ' 200 '

exec 3<>/dev/tcp/${provider.host}/${provider.port} && printf 'GET /realms/plugbricks/.well-known/openid-configuration HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Connection: close

' >&3 && head -n 1 <&3 | grep -q ' 200 '
